claimLevel: I1 (protocol-passed) — reference-client harness, real streams, planted mutants. NOT I2: no index-conformance or position-mapping assertion is made here, and NOT I3: no named editor run is part of this evidence.

declaredAbsence.note: LSP 3.18 mandates Location|null for definition and Location[] for references, so there is NO field on those results a reason could ride. The standard result shapes are UNCHANGED; the reason travels out of band. An empty standard result on these methods must not be read as 'nothing found'.
declaredAbsence.componentContractRead: navigation.ts exposes evidenceTier at this commit, NOT Lane 4's richer absence record (that commit 04d56ab75 is not an ancestor of this branch — see limitations). The reason is derived from the launch set through its single owner, and the vocabulary matches what Lane 4 publishes, so the seam is correct today and still correct when that field lands.

advertisement.note: bb/staleness and bb/impact carry non-standard capability keys (LSP 3.18 has no impactProvider). They ride top-level keys exactly as bb/graph already did via graphProvider, each carrying the schemaVersion the handler ENFORCES, so a client can detect a mismatch before sending one. A client that ignores unknown capability keys can still call them; discoverability is the point, not enforcement.

verdict.note: `failed` counts real functional failures only; mutant runs are reported separately via the verdict block. A mutant caught ONLY by a load failure is reported but does NOT satisfy the suite.

reviewers.separationOfDuties: NOT satisfied for this change: the author of the component change wrote the only gate covering it (contract §8.6 requires cross-review where feasible). Owner spot-check (§8.5) is the closure authority.
reviewers.crossReview: requested from script/m26/verify-graph-transport.ts owner: its M5 mutant anchors on the literal graphProvider line in src/lsp/server.ts, which is why that line was preserved rather than replaced by a table lookup.
reviewers.wave2: This wave's author also wrote the checks covering it. Three defects were found by the wave's own gates on its own code and are recorded rather than hidden: (1) the G11 schemaVersion check compared two reads of the same constant and could not fail — a mutant survived it and the check was rewritten to read the value the client receives; (2) a blanket-catch mutant was first planted as a syntactically broken rewrite and was 'caught' only by load failure, which the suite correctly refused to count, and was replanted as a behaviour change; (3) G3's frame parser decoded the stream to a string and mis-parsed as soon as the advertisement carried a non-ASCII em dash, which the byte-level rewrite fixed.

limitations: single-root workspaces only (multi-root is a filed decision for later waves); declared on the wire as workspace.workspaceFolders.supported = false
no completion, no diagnostics, no rename (complement stance, §7.1)

no textDocumentSync is advertised, because no textDocument/did* handler exists; the declared sync model is filesystem-side (recursive fs.watch, 300 ms debounce, incremental reindex, scan-on-read fallback) and no latency figure is advertised because this gate measures none
stdio framing is byte-stream based with Content-Length parsing
bb/staleness and bb/impact use non-standard capability keys; a client that ignores unknown keys cannot discover them from the initialize result
the mutation suite plants into src/lsp/ and deletes the copy in a finally block; a crash mid-run can leave a server.mutant.<pid>.<n>.ts file behind (git status shows untracked files)
G7 exercises bb/staleness on an UNINDEXED workspace only; the marker shape for a fresh/stale indexed file is freshness.ts's contract, gated by script/m25, not here

NOT VERIFIED: that any editor renders the bb/absence notice. The channel is proven to be emitted and framed on the wire (G3, G9); nothing here proves a client displays it. Claiming a rendered badge would be a §1/I3 claim this evidence does not support

NOT VERIFIED: absence notices for bb/graph, bb/impact, and bb/staleness. Those transports own their own loud `bb/…`-prefixed errors by design (the versioning mechanism) and are not registered absentable; their error text already names the reason

navigation.ts does not yet expose Lane 4's `absence: {reason, language, detail, searchedIndex, totalCount}` record at this commit (04d56ab75 is not an ancestor of lsp/3), so the reason is derived from `evidenceTier` plus the launch set. When that field lands, navigationAbsence() should read it directly; the vocabulary and searchedIndex semantics already match

the DocumentUnroutable type is defined and handled at the seam, but no component throws it yet — document_highlight.ts still lets ASTEngine's own Error propagate and the seam recognises that message. The declared type is the forward-compatible path for other lanes

the seam matches ASTEngine's 'Unsupported file type' message prefix to recognise unroutability. That string is a cross-module coupling to src/ast/engine.ts; if the engine rewords it, the seam degrades to -32603 (loud, not silent) and the mutant 'seam: the unroutable-file guard is removed' fails the suite, so the drift is gated rather than silent
